external_invariants: Model is pretrained Qwen3-4B loaded from the local asset snapshot with dtype=torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation='sdpa', local_files_only=True, in eval mode on context['device'].
Numerical policy matches common.configure(): torch.manual_seed(20261020), matmul/cudnn TF32 disabled, cudnn.benchmark disabled, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', 4 CPU threads, 1 interop thread.
Input is real data: the chat-templated source prompt encoded without special tokens, tiled and truncated to exactly 256 prompt tokens, replicated across batch=1, resident on GPU.
Decoding is greedy argmax over the last-position logits; no sampling, temperature, EOS stopping, or early exit; exactly 32 tokens are generated.
Every forward uses use_cache=True with a KV cache created fresh per run; decode steps feed exactly one token; logits_to_keep=1 as in the source.
ttft boundary is the source's explicit torch.cuda.synchronize() immediately after the first forward/argmax; the workload boundary is the final torch.cuda.synchronize() after the last decode step.
The full workload (prefill plus all 31 decode steps) always executes, in every mode, even though the objective measures only the first-token phase.
Quality comparison uses the source tolerances (atol=rtol=0.02 on logits) and exact greedy token equality; no accuracy or convergence beyond reference fidelity is claimed.
No CUDA initialization or model loading at import time; no second reference model is allocated on GPU; the process group (none here, single process) is never destroyed.

selection.rationale: Objective ttft_ms covers exactly the prefill phase (clean baseline 24.12 ms; 20.9 ms diagnostic prefill CUDA in the trace). The installed region bundle (trial-2cbb71d9a0) owns every pointwise chain in both phases (RMSNorm pow/tail, rope mul/neg/cat/add, silu*mul and the aten mean it invokes), so complementary work must avoid those sites. Within prefill, the only substantial cost outside them is the aten::linear family: 253 calls, 16.73 ms diagnostic, ~80% of prefill CUDA time, split across six prefill-only shape groups: gate/up 9728x2560 (72 calls, 7.80 ms, 108 us each on ampere_bf16_s1688gemm_64x128_sliced1x2), down 2560x9728 (3.74 ms), o_proj (1.74 ms), q_proj (1.50 ms), k/v 1024x2560 (72 calls, 1.11 ms, each running cutlass_80_tensorop splitK plus a cublasLt splitKreduce kernel - 144 launches and workspace round-trips - reaching only ~89 TF vs ~128 TF for sibling GEMM shapes), and lm_head 151936x2560 (833 us on an internal::gemvx matvec streaming 778 MB of weights at ~0.93 TB/s, roughly half of Ampere HBM bandwidth). These six groups are one coherent editable boundary: a single shape-keyed, per-site-gated replacement mechanism for the fixed batch-1x256-token prefill GEMMs, and cross-group edits need one another (a merged q/k/v projection spans the q and k/v groups; gate/up fusion shares the gate/up group). Prefill SDPA (0.82 ms) is excluded to keep the boundary single-mechanism, and all decode-phase work is excluded because it cannot change ttft_ms and decode CUDA graphs/fusion already failed the full-logits gates per previous feedback. No selected group or call intersects the installed bundle, so both implementations remain active.
selection.hypothesis: Shape-specialized replacements for the six frozen prefill GEMM shapes reduce prefill GPU time and therefore ttft_ms: a bandwidth-optimal lm_head matvec (~0.4 ms of the 0.83 ms at observed 0.93 TB/s), a non-splitK k/v path removing 72 reduce launches and workspace traffic (~0.3 ms), and higher-efficiency kernels or merged projections for gate/up/down/o/q running at ~35-40% of Ampere bf16 peak. This is a hypothesis to be tested, not a predicted win: changing GEMM kernel selection alters fp32 accumulation order and previously broke the 0.02 logits/exact-greedy-token gates (trial-9cc583939d gate/up repack), so every custom site must carry build-time numeric gates with per-site fallback to the parent aten::linear (the installed bundle pattern), prove actual custom-path execution via runtime route labels and native trace (the earlier fusion silently fell back on every call), and accept that a quality-gate failure or zero speedup is a valid negative result.

proposal.rationale: This attempt repairs the concrete failures in inputs/previous-feedback.txt within the frozen joint selection (the six prefill aten::linear shape groups; 0 of their 253 call IDs intersect the installed region bundle trial-resample-3896551a-param-102dba91, so the inherited pointwise implementation and this candidate both actually execute). Repair 1 (decode failures): no decode-phase site, CUDA graph, logits wrapper or capture is touched at all; every replacement is a prefill-phase aten::linear site, so the failed decode-graph/fusion class cannot recur and decode stays bit-identical to the parent. Repair 2 (trial-9cc583939d broke the 0.02 logits/exact-greedy gates by repacking gate/up and changing cuBLAS kernel selection/fp32 accumulation order): gate/up (72 sites), down_proj (36), o_proj (36) and q_proj (36) are deliberately left on the parent aten::linear path - 180 of the 253 selected calls return no replacement. Only the two measured-inefficient prefill GEMM families are replaced, each behind layered evidence gates. (a) lm_head prefill matvec ([1,1,2560]x[151936,2560]^T, one call): observed as internal::gemvx streaming 778 MB of weights at ~0.93 TB/s (about half of achievable Ampere DRAM streaming; 833 us of the 24.12 ms baseline); replaced by a warp-per-row CUDA matvec (16-byte vectorized __ldg loads, fp32 accumulation, bf16 round-to-nearest epilogue, same output shape/strides). Expected ~490-560 us, i.e. ~0.3 ms off ttft_ms; it is the last projection before the compared logits, so there is no through-layer amplification and differences are bounded at ~1 bf16 ULP (always inside atol=rtol=0.02). (b) k_proj/v_proj prefill GEMMs (72 calls): observed as one cutlass_80_tensorop splitK plus one cublasLt splitKreduce kernel per call (144 launches and workspace round-trips at ~86 TF vs ~128 TF for sibling shapes); replaced by ONE merged cuBLAS GEMM per layer over an invariant packed [Wk;Wv] (2048x2560) weight built once per physical module. The k_proj call computes the merged GEMM and returns the k half as a view while stashing the v half keyed by the shared input tensor identity (consume-once registry with strong references, the installed bundle's own pattern); the v_proj call returns the stashed v half after verifying input and weight identity, otherwise computes the parent reference. No call is eliminated (eliminated_calls is empty): the v_proj calls still execute and return data the framework can observe. Downstream consumers stay valid because Qwen3-4B attention only splits the last projection dimension (k_proj(x).view(bsz,q_len,kv_heads,head_dim) is a legal pure split of the row-strided slice), SDPA/rope/cache ops are stride-agnostic, and the installed bundle's RMSNorm/rope guards handle strided inputs or fall back to bit-exact aten paths. Unlike the earlier fusion that fell back silently on every call, actual custom-path execution is self-reported per invocation via record_route labels (lmhead_matvec / lmhead_first_call_ok / kv_merge_fused / kv_merge_consume, with explicit lmhead_parent / kv_parent / *_reject fallback labels) and remains subject to the framework's independent call counting and trace evidence. Every custom path must pass a build-time numeric gate against the parent operator (atol=rtol=2^-7 on synthetic operands), a build-time speed gate (matvec <0.85x parent median; merged KV <0.88x separate medians, else the cuBLAS heuristic lost and the sites stay on the parent), and a per-site first-call live numeric comparison against the parent reference with permanent per-site fallback; any exception or signature mismatch (shape/dtype/contiguity/bias) falls back to the parent callable. Expected effect is ~0.4-0.7 ms off the 24.12 ms ttft (~2-3%); this is a hypothesis to be tested by the paired project measurements, and a quality-gate failure or zero speedup is an accepted negative result. Nothing about batch, sequence length, token counts, sampling, data, completion boundary or thresholds is altered, no fixture outputs are precomputed or cached, and the workload executes fully on every invocation.

setup_work.packed_kv_weights: 36 x torch.cat([k_proj.weight, v_proj.weight], dim=0) -> contiguous [2048,2560] bf16, built once per physical attention module during build under torch.no_grad() after shape/dtype/contiguity/device checks; 377,487,360 bytes (36 x 10.49 MB) retained for the warm inference-only model lifetime (weights are invariant; no optimizer or gradient state exists). The original module weights are left untouched so the exact parent fallback path stays available. This retained setup allocation raises the per-run peak_allocated floor and framework lifecycle peaks by the same amount; the per-layer cat transient (~10.5 MB, sequential) briefly adds to lifecycle peak only.
setup_work.inline_extension: opop_prefill_gemm_v1 CUDA extension (single lmhead_matvec kernel, warp-per-row, 256 threads/block, 18992 blocks for N=151936) compiled once at build via torch.utils.cpp_extension.load_inline with TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST pinned to the worker device capability; compile artifacts live in the torch extension cache (non-PyTorch driver allocation not covered by any memory counter).
setup_work.build_time_gates: Run on the worker device before enabling any custom path: numeric comparisons against torch.nn.functional.linear on seeded synthetic operands (three input scales for the matvec; both k and v halves for the merged KV GEMM) at atol=rtol=2^-7, plus median wall-time speed gates over 20 iterations after 5 warmups (matvec must be <0.85x parent, merged KV <0.88x the two separate GEMMs). Total cost is a few hundred milliseconds of one-time GPU work during setup; failures disable the custom path while the callables remain installed as honest parent-routing replacements.
setup_work.first_call_verification: On the first invocation of each replaced site the custom result is compared against the live parent reference result (atol=rtol=2^-7) and the site permanently falls back to the parent on mismatch; this costs one extra parent GEMM per site (~31 us per KV site, ~833 us for lm_head) during the first quality/warm invocation only. Decisions are per-site booleans, never cached tensor outputs.
setup_work.state_and_synchronization: No streams, graphs, collectives or cross-call ordering changes are introduced: within each layer the k_proj replacement still runs at its original call position and the v_proj replacement returns at its original position, on the current stream, so the installed bundle's pointwise chain and all consumers observe unchanged ordering. The consume-once stash holds strong references only between the adjacent k_proj and v_proj calls of one layer forward.

quality_risks: Changed GEMM accumulation order (merged cuBLAS KV kernel; custom lm_head matvec) produces bf16 ULP-level output differences that can amplify through the 36 layers and the persisted KV cache into the 0.02 logits / exact-greedy-token gates - the same failure class as trial-9cc583939d. Mitigations: gate/up/down/o/q stay on the parent path; only k/v (measured splitK-inefficient) and the terminal lm_head (no downstream amplification) are replaced; build-time and per-site first-call numeric gates with permanent fallback bound each site to ~1 bf16 ULP versus the parent on live data. A full-logits failure remains possible and would be reported as a negative result.

Greedy argmax near-ties: the prefill lm_head and KV perturbations could flip the first decoded token if the top-2 logit gap is below ~1 bf16 ULP; tokens are checked exactly, so any flip fails quality rather than being masked.

k/v halves are returned as non-contiguous views of the merged [*,2048] GEMM output. The downstream Qwen3 view is a legal pure split of the last dimension and later ops are stride-agnostic, and the installed bundle handles strided inputs or falls back bit-exactly, but any unanticipated stride-sensitive consumer would exercise the parent path (correct, slower). No in-place rewrite of any parent tensor occurs.

The merged KV cuBLAS kernel selection is decided by cuBLAS heuristics: if it is not faster than the observed splitK pair on the worker device, the build-time speed gate disables the KV merge entirely (candidate then reduces to the lm_head site; zero speedup is a valid negative result).

The lm_head kernel requires K%256==0 and 16-byte-aligned contiguous bf16 operands and bias=None; any other signature falls back to the parent aten::linear, and kernel launch errors are caught and routed to the parent.

Route labels and first-call checks prove custom-path execution and per-site numeric agreement with the parent at ULP scale, but they do not by themselves prove end-to-end logits equivalence; that remains the framework's full-logits and exact-greedy-token gates.
